beats.what_happened: Fifteen years after being struck off, Mervyn typed another man's order and was sent out of the chamber to wait.

state_changes.fact: He is publicly reduced from legal professional to paid typist.

beats.what_happened: Irfan mistook Mervyn for an official who could hear his urgent housing dispute, and Mervyn examined the file without correcting him.

state_changes.fact: He believes Mervyn has authority to hear urgent matters.
He experiences public deference for the first time in years.

beats.what_happened: Irfan touched Mervyn's feet and asked him to hear the case.

state_changes.fact: He is directly invited to exercise judicial authority again.
He places his mother's housing dispute in Mervyn's hands.

beats.what_happened: Mervyn called his intervention advice, typed a direction in judicial form and signed it as presiding officer.

state_changes.fact: He creates his first signed direction for a private litigant.
He receives a paper intended to compel restoration of the room.

beats.what_happened: Irfan presented Mervyn's signed page, and the landlord restored the key and paid six thousand rupees without court proceedings.

state_changes.fact: His mother regains access and the full advance payment.
It produces voluntary compliance despite lacking a seal or case number.

beats.what_happened: A copy of Mervyn's first signed direction remained preserved with the housing papers after payment.

state_changes.fact: A discoverable copy survives after the dispute is resolved.

beats.note: No cast character observes where the retained copy is stored, leaving its future chain of discovery open.

beats.what_happened: Irfan returned to Mervyn with two more men, their files and their fees.

state_changes.fact: His one intervention becomes a potential paid practice.
He becomes the source of Mervyn's first referrals.

beats.location: court canteen and room above tyre shop
beats.what_happened: Mervyn accepted the two referrals and used their fees to rent a room above a tyre shop.

state_changes.fact: He acquires a dedicated location for hearing disputes.
A private rented room becomes the base of the operation.

beats.what_happened: Mervyn installed an eight-inch dais and a nameplate identifying an arbitration and dispute resolution forum with a presiding officer.

state_changes.fact: It gains the visible furniture and signage of an adjudicatory office.
He is publicly addressed as sir by the property owner.

beats.what_happened: Vaishali questioned who appointed Mervyn, and he said private parties would appoint an arbitrator by consent.

state_changes.fact: She knows Mervyn has opened a private dispute forum with a dais.
He states that the record he creates will reflect party consent.

beats.what_happened: Mervyn hired Sarika for three thousand rupees per month, designated her registry clerk and obtained her signature certifying proceedings recorded by her.

state_changes.fact: She begins her first office job as registry clerk.
Her signature is attached to certification language she does not fully understand.
He gains a clerk who can make the room function like a formal forum.

beats.what_happened: After Mervyn conducted the first two numbered matters, an unknown stranger entered unannounced and placed a heavy file on Sarika's desk.

state_changes.fact: It begins attracting litigants beyond Irfan's direct referrals.
His operation receives its first unsolicited matter.

beats.what_happened: Dhawale brought a land dispute concerning property valued at one crore forty lakh and pressed Mervyn for an urgent ruling.

state_changes.fact: placed a high-value land dispute before Mervyn
accepted his largest matter to date for hearing

beats.what_happened: The landowner appeared with the advocate, signed a consent memorandum and argued the land dispute before Mervyn.

state_changes.fact: observed Mervyn conduct a high-value hearing under a signed consent memorandum
recorded the parties' consent and proceedings

beats.what_happened: Mervyn ordered conveyance at the contracted price, and the landowner accepted the balance payment while the advocate stated that his client would comply.

state_changes.fact: issued an award that the losing party publicly agreed to obey
secured an enforceable signed resolution for the land purchase
acknowledged that the ruling held because his client had consented and accepted payment

beats.what_happened: A copy of the signed consent memorandum and award was preserved with the land transaction papers.

state_changes.fact: now contains documentary evidence of Mervyn's award

beats.note: No cast character perceived the records handling, leaving the location and future path of the preserved copy open.

beats.what_happened: Mervyn admitted there was no prior appointment order, and the advocate warned that another lawyer could challenge the room before consenting.

state_changes.fact: recognized that comparison with formal court records could expose his forum
learned that Mervyn had no prior appointment order for the matter

beats.what_happened: Mervyn asked Pandit for access to the civil pending list so he could avoid disputes already filed in the real court, and Pandit refused cash.

state_changes.fact: learned why Mervyn needed the pending list
sought confidential registry information to screen future cases

beats.what_happened: Pandit left the pending list on a rear photocopier long enough for Mervyn to photograph all thirty-two pages.

state_changes.fact: obtained the real court's current pending list
began leaking confidential registry information to Mervyn

beats.what_happened: Pandit demanded one sealed envelope each month, to be opened by Mervyn without questions, as the price of continued access.

state_changes.fact: made continued leaks conditional on a monthly sealed envelope
became indebted to Pandit on undisclosed terms

beats.what_happened: Manjula sought an urgent hearing over land and keys withheld by Bhaskar for eleven years, and Mervyn fixed the hearing for eight days later.

state_changes.fact: obtained a hearing before Bhaskar could place a tenant on the land
was required to answer his sister's claim publicly

beats.what_happened: At the hearing, Mervyn established that Manjula held an equal recorded share while Bhaskar controlled all access and had not fully accounted for crop income.

state_changes.fact: failed to justify excluding Manjula from jointly recorded property
proved her recorded ownership and lack of access

beats.what_happened: Mervyn awarded Manjula access and possession according to her recorded share, barred Bhaskar from leasing the western half and ordered delivery of the keys.

state_changes.fact: received judgment granting access and possession of her share
was ordered to surrender the keys and provide accounts
issued a judgment that protected Manjula's recorded ownership

beats.what_happened: Bhaskar delivered both keys under the judgment, and Manjula publicly told the lane that a court had finally listened to her.

state_changes.fact: gained physical access to the land and storage room after eleven years
publicly acknowledged that he was obeying the court's judgment
had a second ruling obeyed outside his hearing room

beats.what_happened: Harshad received a filing bundle containing an award from an unfamiliar forum and directed that its authority be traced.

state_changes.fact: became aware of an award issued under an unrecognized forum name
entered district court scrutiny as an attached award

beats.what_happened: Harshad found no matching forum, appointment, arbitrator name or case-number sequence in the available district records.

state_changes.fact: could not trace the forum or case number in district records
lacked a traceable appointing record

beats.what_happened: The complete filing bundle remained routed for further scrutiny rather than being returned at the public counter.

state_changes.fact: remained preserved in the district court scrutiny process

beats.note: No cast character witnessed the internal routing step; it remains deliberate open canon established by the file's continued presence.

beats.what_happened: Harshad wrote the unidentified case number on a slip and stored it in his drawer for further inquiry.

state_changes.fact: opened a personal inquiry into case one seven six
became the unknowing subject of registry scrutiny

beats.what_happened: The advocate publicly challenged Sarika to explain what her certification signature represented and reminded Mervyn that no prior appointment order had been produced.

state_changes.fact: learned publicly that her certification could be treated as proof of proceedings she had not fully recorded
lost control of how Sarika understood her registry role

beats.what_happened: Mervyn admitted that he established the forum himself and could not identify an external order appointing him as presiding officer.

state_changes.fact: understood that Mervyn had no external appointment order
could no longer rely on Sarika's ignorance of the forum's status

beats.what_happened: Sarika counted fourteen months of salary envelopes and recognized that her signatures had travelled on certified copies outside the room.

state_changes.fact: recognized the possible legal exposure attached to fourteen months of certifications
ceased to regard the clerk position as unquestionably respectable

beats.what_happened: Sarika asked Mervyn whether she could be jailed for her role.

state_changes.fact: directly confronted Mervyn about criminal liability
was required to face the personal cost imposed on his clerk

beats.what_happened: Mervyn received Harshad's written demand for his appointment order and learned that he had eleven days to respond.

state_changes.fact: faced an eleven-day deadline to produce a nonexistent appointment order
learned that the district court was formally scrutinizing an award
formally sought documentary proof of the forum's authority

beats.what_happened: Mervyn asked Pandit to insert a false appointment into an old court record, and Pandit identified the request as forgery.

state_changes.fact: attempted to obtain a fabricated historical appointment record
refused to share the risk of altering a court register

beats.what_happened: Pandit stated that each sealed envelope contained a dispute and required outcome, and that Mervyn had signed twelve awards preserving those outcomes.

state_changes.fact: recognized that access to the pending list had cost him twelve controlled rulings
held specific leverage connecting Mervyn to predetermined outcomes
were revealed to contain cases and requested operative results rather than money

beats.what_happened: Pandit refused to assist with the appointment order and demanded the return of the photographed pending list.

state_changes.fact: lost Pandit's assistance while the registry deadline remained active
ended the pending-list arrangement and sought recovery of the leaked material

beats.what_happened: Mervyn began his largest hearing before a packed room while Tejas watched from the back.

state_changes.fact: saw Mervyn publicly treated as a judicial authority
reached the largest public display of his false authority

beats.what_happened: Sarika publicly refused to certify an exhibit while Mervyn continued the hearing.

state_changes.fact: ceased certifying documents for Mervyn
lost his clerk's public compliance
saw Sarika express fear about the legitimacy of her work

beats.what_happened: Dhawale produced a prewritten outcome and copies of twelve earlier awards, then demanded that Mervyn award him the western parcel at two crore ten lakh rupees.

state_changes.fact: openly asserted control over Mervyn's next ruling
was publicly exposed as vulnerable to dictated outcomes
heard evidence that Mervyn's rulings were controlled

beats.what_happened: After the room cleared, Tejas asked Mervyn which court had appointed him.

state_changes.fact: directly questioned the source of Mervyn's authority
could no longer conceal the appointment question from his son

beats.what_happened: Harshad verified across current, retired and section records that no appointed arbitrator, appointment order, constituted tribunal or official case-number sequence matched Mervyn's forum.

state_changes.fact: established from court records that Mervyn had no recorded appointment or tribunal
his claimed authority failed formal verification

beats.what_happened: Harshad signed a police complaint supported by the verification note, the bar record and copies of thirty-four awards.

state_changes.fact: converted the records inquiry into a criminal complaint
became the named subject of a police complaint

beats.what_happened: A sealed police copy of the verification note and award index remained preserved for investigation.

state_changes.fact: contained a preserved verification note and index of awards

beats.note: No cast character witnessed the secured evidence copy being stored, preserving its custody as deliberate open canon.

beats.what_happened: Khot told Sarika she was named as an employee and witness rather than an accused, and Sarika disclosed the location of the forum's records.

state_changes.fact: was treated as a cooperating witness rather than arrested
gained access to three cartons of forum records

beats.what_happened: Khot read aloud the charge that Mervyn cheated people by falsely representing judicial authority and inducing transfers through purported awards.

state_changes.fact: was taken into police custody on a cheating allegation based on false judicial authority
learned publicly that no court appointment supported his father's forum

beats.what_happened: Khot offered to record Mervyn's cooperation for a narrower prosecution position if he listed every award and admitted that each lacked judicial force.

state_changes.fact: was offered possible leniency in exchange for disavowing all awards
began receiving Mervyn's statement identifying affected matters

beats.what_happened: Mervyn identified the earlier matters, admitted he lacked court appointment and stated that the first twenty-three awards had no judicial force.

state_changes.fact: formally disavowed his authority for the first twenty-three matters
gained Mervyn's partial admission and award list

beats.what_happened: Mervyn refused to call Manjula's award worthless despite being told that the refusal could cost him leniency.

state_changes.fact: sacrificed possible leniency rather than disavow Manjula's judgment
recorded only partial cooperation through matter twenty-three
her award was omitted from Mervyn's disavowal list

beats.what_happened: Manjula remained in possession of both keys and was not told about Mervyn's arrest or the challenge to his authority.

state_changes.fact: still held both keys without knowing that Mervyn's authority had been exposed
